title: Nonzero tensor product of finite modules over a local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring with residue field $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$. If $M$ and $N$ are nonzero finitely generated $R$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], then $M\otimes_RN\ne0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 00DV (Nakayama lemma), together with the tensor-product base-change isomorphism of Section 010Z

proof.text: Put $\overline M=M/\mathfrak mM$ and $\overline N=N/\mathfrak mN$. They are $\kappa$-vector spaces, with $[r][x]=[rx]$: the formula is well-defined since $\mathfrak m$ kills each quotient. If $\overline M=0$, the image of the zero submodule of $M$ is all of $M/\mathfrak mM$; the final assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] then gives $M=0$, a contradiction. Its hypotheses hold because $R$ is local and $M$ is finitely generated. The identical application to the finite module $N$ proves $\overline N\ne0$. Thus both residue quotients are nonzero.

source.place: Tag 00DV, lemma-NAK, parts (2) and (4), applied to the zero submodule and the maximal ideal.

proof.text: The residue ring $\kappa$ is a field by the hypothesis that $\mathfrak m$ is maximal. Apply [lem-pur-field-vector-space-tensor-nontrivial] to the two nonzero $\kappa$-modules from Step 1. It gives $T=\overline M\otimes_\kappa\overline N\ne0$. No freeness or flatness over $R$ is required.

source.place: Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_nontrivial, lines 114-117, with the nontrivial-free faithfully-flat instance at line 209 and Module.Free.of_divisionRing (Basis/VectorSpace.lean:156).

proof.text: Regard $T$ as an $R$-module through $R\to\kappa$. The map $\beta:M\times N\to T$, $(x,y)\mapsto[x]\otimes[y]$, is $R$-bilinear: additivity follows from the quotient maps and tensor relations, and $[rx]\otimes[y]=[r]([x]\otimes[y])=[x]\otimes[ry]$. By the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], it induces $q:M\otimes_RN\to T$ sending $x\otimes y$ to $[x]\otimes[y]$. This map is surjective: every element of $T$ is a finite sum of pure tensors after absorbing scalar coefficients into the first factor, and every such pure tensor lifts by choosing representatives in $M$ and $N$. If $M\otimes_RN=0$, this surjection would give $T=0$, contradicting Step 2. Hence $M\otimes_RN\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, universal property and generation by pure tensors in its proof; the quotient bilinear map and its surjectivity are written out here.
